I've been looking into this game for a while. How does it compare to Ninja Gaiden? Am I crazy for seeing a resemblance?

Ninja Gaiden was a hard game, but it's a different kind of "hard". NG's hard was (mostly) because of increasing level complexity which required the user to master twitch muscle memory. Dark Souls' kind of hard is due to the creator's ideals about a struggle along a journey which was intentionally designed to stop the user from just rushing in and thrashing at everything to win. DS' hard is usually experienced as sudden and unforseen death coupled with the requirement that the user must figure out (no help given, not even an explanation of the UI) the entire game and every new twist and turn that gets thrown their way. DS is arguably one of the best games of all time.

saddens me that every time some one takes the time to do a test like this they seem to mess up the methodology. These guys are close but the speed is not the issue. The main problem with it registering correctly is moving the sword to the correct starting position before attempting to initiate a slash. The trick is a vertical slash has all the same forward momentum of a stab. so if the distance of the swipe isnt high enough or the starting position is wrong it will think you stabbing. I did bump into the occasional error when I played but pretty much every time I knew why it happened and mostly i needed to calm down.

I'd be willing to bet plenty of people play through this game without errors or need to recalibrate. There are probably speed runners out there who have mastered it. The issue is more that the game is just not as button-masher / incorrect input friendly as people expect, especially from a nintendo game.

Speed definitely factors. If you wave around like a maniac obviously he wont follow. The swiping distance however wasn't noted. I definitely agree that's its more player error than game error, and that you have to be willing to learn what the game wants but there's definitely a little fuzzy logic in there.
